brief: Goldman Sachs frames agentic AI as reshaping the consumer shopping journey, moving from today's discovery/research use toward gradual end-to-end autonomous purchasing over 3-5+ years, not an overnight shift. Central thesis: value follows consumer intent, so the strategic question shifts from who owns the storefront to who owns discovery, intent and the payment infrastructure that converts intent into a transaction. This creates opportunities across eCommerce, advertising, payments and cybersecurity, and opens debates on customer ownership, distribution economics, merchant margins and liability. GS sizes $2.6tn of US spending in high-likelihood categories, estimating roughly 2% agentic penetration of that card-present spend could add about 1 percentage point to eCommerce growth, with $12.3tn in high-and-medium-likelihood volume overall. Card networks Visa and Mastercard are seen as the default payment rail via tokenization, Meta and Google as distribution winners, Equifax, TransUnion and FICO as identity/fraud infrastructure beneficiaries, and Amazon, Walmart and Shopify as retail winners on price/scale. Primary ticketing (Live Nation) is favored over secondary (StubHub) on differentiated inventory. GS names META, GOOGL, AMZN, V, MA, EFX, TRU, FICO, LYV, SHOP, NET, STUB, WMT, SN and TPR as positively skewed to the theme, despite some (EFX, TRU) carrying Neutral ratings.
